title: Find Peak Element
statement:
Given a 0-indexed array of N integers, a peak element is an element that is strictly greater than its neighbors. For elements at the boundaries, we assume A[-1] = -∞ and A[N] = -∞.

Find the 0-indexed position of any peak element. If the array contains multiple peaks, return the index to any of the peaks.

You must solve this in O(log N) using binary search by comparing A[mid] with A[mid+1].
inputFormat:
Line 1: a single integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer: the index of a peak element.

examples.explanation: 3 is a peak since 3 > 2 and 3 > 1. Index is 2.
6 is a peak (index 5). 2 is also a peak (index 1). Either 1 or 5 works (the checker will accept either, but for this problem, your binary search should naturally find one).
